title: session-classifier-mini-prd-and-experiment-notes
content:
High-level idea:

We build a lightweight, real-time session classifier that infers a session's expected fidelity requirements and routing preference early in the session (first N turns or metadata). The classifier output is used by runtime routing to:
  - select a model tier (cheap/medium/premium)
  - choose context retention policy (full-prefix, compact-summary, ephemeral-only)
  - set caching prefixes / KV cache warmup heuristics
  - optionally route to dedicated capacity for high-throughput, SLA sessions

Why this?
  - Many apps have predictable session-level patterns (e.g., data ingestion bots vs. creative writing). Picking per-session config reduces token cost and improves SLOs vs per-request heuristics.
  - We can proactively warm caches or prefetch embeddings for sessions likely to need them.
  - Provides a simple guardrail for progressive-fidelity fallbacks and cheaper baseline routing.

Non-goals (for v0):
  - No heavy on-device ML or per-user personalization.
  - Not replacing per-request reranking or RLHF quality checks.

Inputs available for classification:
  - session metadata (client app, plan, region, device type)
  - first 1-3 user messages (token-limited text + length and intent features)
  - historical session-level signal (if session id maps to user with prior sessions, optional)
  - explicit user/agent hint (e.g., `priority:high` header)

Output labels (coarse):
  - fidelity_tier: [economy, balanced, fidelity]
  - retention_policy: [full, compact, ephemeral]
  - route_hint: [hosted-lowcost, hosted-standard, dedicated-small, dedicated-large]
  - prefetch_actions: [none, embed_prefetch, prefix_cache, kv_warmup]

User stories (rough):
  - As a product engineer, I want sessions that are clearly transactional (short intent, high frequency) to default to economy tier so my overall token bill drops without hurting UX.
  - As an SRE, I want to identify sessions that will likely spike tokens so we can pre-allocate capacity (avoid cold-batch penalties).
  - As a solutions engineer, I want to allow customers to opt-out or pin classifier decisions per-organization (compliance/consistency).

Acceptance criteria (v0):
  - Classifier runs inline in the router with <6ms median added latency on hosted path (p95 <20ms) for first-request inference.
  - Initial classifier accuracy on label 'economy' vs others >= 80% on internal eval set (balanced across 8 app categories).
  - Routing changes applied on session-level and persisted for session lifetime (config TTL = 24h).
  - Metrics surfaced in Console: % sessions by predicted tier, cost delta per cohort, rollbackable per-customer flag.

Data / Eval plan:
  - Collect a 30k-session scrape from opt-in customers + synthetic sessions from test harness. Label heuristics: token-length, follow-up rate, user action conversion as proxies for fidelity need.
  - Offline eval: precision/recall per label and business-metric sim (cost saved vs quality regressions measured by A/B prompts).
  - Online experiment: feature-flagged A/B for 10% of traffic for 4 weeks, monitor latency SLOs, conversion/quality proxies, and cost delta.

Experiment design (A/B):
  - A: baseline routing (no classifier).
  - B: classifier decides tier + retention.
  - Metrics: per-session avg tokens, 75/95 latency, user satisfaction proxies (if app provides), downstream conversion (if available), error rate, fallback invocations.

Architecture sketch (runtime):
  1) Client opens session / first request reaches gateway.
  2) Router calls classifier service (light HTTP RPC) with first-turn snapshot.
  3) Classifier returns labels and confidence score.
  4) Router applies a decision policy (policy can override low-confidence to default to safer tier).
  5) Router tags request and subsequent requests in session with policy; persistence via session-store.

Operational controls / admin UX:
  - Per-customer toggle: force classifier off / pin tier.
  - Confidence threshold knob in Console to bias conservative routing.
  - Per-route override rules (e.g., routes under /inference/enterprise always map to fidelity).

Privacy / compliance notes:
  - Default: stateless classifier uses only first-turn token window and metadata, does not persist raw text beyond short-term session-store TTL.
  - For customers requiring zero-text retention, provide a policy to bypass classifier and use explicit routing headers.

Open questions / risks:
  - Cold-start bias: first-turn content may be sparse or ambiguous, causing misclassification. Mitigation: backoff policy, request for explicit hint via header.
  - Edge-case churn: chatbots that transition from economy -> fidelity mid-session. Need per-message re-eval trigger (cost vs complexity tradeoff).
  - Auditability: customers will want to see why a session was labeled a certain way. We need human-readable explanations, at least label + top features.

Implementation milestones (proposal):
  - Week 0-2: proto classifier (logistic/decision tree) + offline eval on harvested sessions.
  - Week 3-5: runtime integration prototype behind feature flag, end-to-end smoke tests, low-traffic canary.
  - Week 6-9: A/B experiment, Console metrics surfaces, per-customer controls.
  - Week 10+: iterate on model, introduce per-message re-eval only for high-confidence transitions.

Fallback and rollback strategy:
  - Default to baseline routing on classifier service errors.
  - Feature-flag at router-level to immediately disable routing changes.
  - Auto-rollback if p95 latency regression > 10% or error rate increases > 0.5% above baseline.

Notes to self / TODOs:
  - Ask Kai for the event schema for session-store (what fields persist).
  - Build a small labeling tool to annotate 2k sessions quickly for initial training.
  - Add a simple explainer in the Console (why did this session go to economy?).
  - Check legal re: retaining first-turn text even transiently (privacy team).

Short-term experiment idea: 'one-click hint' header (x-redwood-priority) where client can declare intent; measure mismatch rate between declared intent and classifier. Use as signal for hybrid approach (client-hint + classifier).

Longer-term thoughts (beyond v0):
  - Personalization layer: per-customer / per-workspace classifiers trained on their traffic patterns.
  - Multi-label outputs: score expected hallucination risk, expected tokens, and expected latency separately to enable multi-dimensional routing.
  - Integrate with Optimize to recommend quantization/profile changes for sessions predicted to be long-running.

Rough resource asks:
  - 0.5 SWE (router integration) + 0.5 ML eng (prototype classifier) for 6 weeks.
  - 0.25 PM to run experiment, coordinate with Console and legal.

Endnotes: keep v0 conservative and very observable. The biggest win is driving down tokens on obvious short transactional sessions without touching customer-facing quality for fidelity cases.
